user.title: How should powerplan help?
user.description:
Three ways to run, and you can change your mind later.

**Price and capacity** — shift load to cheap hours *and* keep every hour under your grid company's capacity step. This is what most Norwegian houses want.

**Price only** — follow the price and ignore capacity. Choose this if your grid company has no capacity component, or if you have no meter reading powerplan can use.

**Fuse only** — no prices, no tariff: just never trip the main fuse while several big loads run at once.

name.title: Name this site
name.description: A site is one grid connection: its meter, its prices and its capacity tariff.

data_description.name: What to call this grid connection. It names the site device and prefixes its entities.

timezone.title: Which timezone is the house in?
timezone.description: powerplan normally takes this from your Home Assistant settings, but yours has no timezone set. Everything with a time in it — window boundaries, day and night, deadlines, when tomorrow's prices are due — depends on this answer.

data_description.timezone: The IANA zone the house is in.

electrical.title: Your grid connection
electrical.description: Four questions about the physical connection. The answers fix what the house can draw and how amps become watts; the review step shows the result in kW so you can check it.

data_description.country: Taken from your Home Assistant settings. It sets the defaults below.
data_description.system: Look in the fuse box: an IT system has three wires and no neutral, a TN system has a neutral. Both are common in Norway.
data_description.phases: How many phases the house is connected with.
data_description.main_fuse_a: The rating of the main fuse, in amps. It is printed on the fuse or on your grid agreement.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Already filled in. Open it only if you know you want something else.

data_description.per_phase_limit_a: Advanced: a lower limit per phase than the main fuse, if your grid company set one. Defaults to the main fuse.

meter.title: Which device is your meter?
meter.description: Pick the device that reads your grid meter — an AMS/HAN reader, a P1 dongle, a Tibber Pulse — and powerplan fills in the sensors it finds on it. Leave it empty to pick the sensors yourself.

data_description.device: Optional. Only used to suggest the sensors on the next step.

meter_roles.title: What each meter sensor is
meter_roles.description: Check what powerplan found. Grid power and the import register are the two that matter: power is how fast the house is drawing, the register is what closes each capacity window exactly. Everything else is optional.

data_description.grid_power: The meter's power reading for the whole house. Import is positive, export negative.
data_description.import_register: The meter's total imported energy. This is what closes each window exactly.
data_description.export_register: The meter's total exported energy, if you have production. Optional.
data_description.production_power: What your panels or other production are producing right now. Optional.
data_description.meter_window: Some meters publish the running hour's consumption themselves. Optional.
data_description.phase_current_l1: Per-phase current, in amps. Optional, and only useful with all three.

prices.title: Where do your prices come from?
prices.description: powerplan needs tomorrow's prices to plan tonight. Pick whichever you already have.

data_description.source: Nord Pool is read through the official integration; a sensor is anything that already publishes a price curve.

prices_nordpool.title: Nord Pool
prices_nordpool.description: powerplan asks the Nord Pool integration for each day's prices; it never calls the market itself. Tomorrow's auction result usually lands early in the afternoon, market time.

data_description.config_entry: Which Nord Pool entry to read prices through.
data_description.area: The bidding area the house is in.
data_description.currency: The currency to ask for, normally your own.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Already filled in. Open it only if you know you want something else.

data_description.publication_tz: Advanced: the time zone the market publishes in. Derived from the price area; leave empty to keep that.
data_description.publication_time: Advanced: the local time tomorrow's prices usually appear. Derived from the price area; leave empty to keep that.

prices_entity.title: Your price sensor
prices_entity.description: Pick the sensor that already carries a price curve. powerplan recognises the common formats and tells you which one it detected.

data_description.entity_id: The sensor whose attributes hold the hours and their prices.
data_description.format: Detected from the integration that owns the sensor. Change it only if the prices come out wrong.

prices_fixed.title: Your fixed price
prices_fixed.description: With no curve to follow, powerplan cannot move load to a cheaper hour — but it still costs your energy and defends your capacity target.

data_description.price: What you pay for a kilowatt-hour.

modifiers.title: What is added on top?
modifiers.description: The spot price is not what you pay. Tick what applies to you; each one asks its own short question next. Your grid company's energy charge comes from the tariff you choose later, with its numbers and their source, so you do not have to type it.

data_description.modifiers: Everything powerplan can add to a raw price. Leave one out and it is simply not part of your price.

modifier_options.title: {modifier}
modifier_options.description: The numbers for this one. Every field has a default; change what you know.

data_description.amount: In your currency, per kWh. A negative amount is allowed.
data_description.periods: The day and night periods and their prices. The tariff preset fills these in for you.
data_description.fallback: What to use for an hour no period covers.
data_description.cap_kwh_per_month: How many kWh a month the fixed price covers; spot applies above it.
data_description.threshold: The price per kWh above which the state pays a share.
data_description.mult: Your supplier's factor on the spot price. 1 is no change.
data_description.offset: Added to every kWh, in your currency.
data_description.tiers: The monthly use bands and their prices.
data_description.basis: Whether the tiers count a month's use or a year's.
data_description.rates: The announced day types and what each one costs.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Already filled in. Open it only if you know you want something else.

data_description.applies_to: Which price components VAT is charged on. Leave empty for all of them.
data_description.months: The month numbers this applies in. Leave empty for the whole year.
data_description.applies_above_mtd_kwh: kWh this calendar month before the charge starts. Leave empty for always.
data_description.negative_rule: What the scheme does when the spot price is below zero.

export.title: Do you sell electricity back?
export.description: If you export, what you are paid for it decides whether charging the battery beats selling. A negative export price is possible and powerplan does not hide it.

data_description.mode: How your supplier pays for what you send out.
data_description.amount: The fixed price, or what is subtracted from spot.
data_description.share: As a fraction: 0.9 is 90 % of spot.

carriers.title: Any other energy carriers?
carriers.description: A heat pump competes with whatever else heats the house. Tick anything you buy as well as electricity; leave it empty if electricity is all you have.

data_description.carriers: Each one asks for its price next.

data_description.mode: A number you type, or a sensor read once a day.
data_description.price: In your currency, per kWh of delivered energy.
data_description.entity_id: The sensor holding today's price, if you chose a sensor.

tariff.title: Who is your grid company?
tariff.description: The capacity part of your grid bill is what powerplan is mostly for. Pick your grid company and the next step shows, in plain words, what powerplan thinks they bill you — check it against your own invoice.

data_description.preset: Pick yours, or Custom to describe the tariff yourself. If you are not sure, the generic choice is a safe start and you can change it later.

tariff_preset.title: Is this your bill?

tariff_target.title: What should powerplan defend?
tariff_target.description: The target is the ceiling powerplan keeps each hour under. Automatic defends the step you are already in this month, which is the right answer until you know your own pattern.

data_description.target: Automatic, or a specific step with its monthly fee.
data_description.risk: Your grid company bills the average of your three highest hours, so hours under today's peak are already paid for. Using them costs nothing.
data_description.target_kw: The kW to defend, for a tariff with no steps.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Already filled in. Open it only if you know you want something else.

data_description.eps_kwh: Advanced: kWh of the window held back for meter delay and reaction time. kWh, not watts.
data_description.cap_margin_kw: Advanced: how far above the target the free ride may reach.

tariff_bills.title: Your last twelve months
tariff_bills.description: This tariff averages over a rolling year, so powerplan needs what you have already used. Fill in what you can find on your invoices; every field is optional and powerplan says when it knows too little.

data_description.month_1: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_2: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_3: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_4: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_5: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_6: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_7: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_8: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_9: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_10: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_11: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_12: The highest measured value that month, in kW.

tariff_limits.title: Your contracted power
tariff_limits.description: This tariff contracts a power limit per period. The values come from the tariff; change them to what your own contract says.

data_description.limit_1: The contracted power for this period.
data_description.limit_2: The contracted power for this period.
data_description.limit_3: The contracted power for this period.
data_description.limit_4: The contracted power for this period.

hard_limits.title: The hard limit
hard_limits.description: The line powerplan never crosses, whatever the price or the tariff says. It defaults to what your main fuse can deliver.

data_description.contracted_kw: kW the whole house may draw at once.

presence.title: Is anyone home?
presence.description: Comfort matters less in an empty house. powerplan can follow your Home Assistant people, or leave presence to you and your automations.

data_description.mode: Automatic follows the people below; manual leaves it to a service call or the presence entity.
data_description.persons: Everyone whose being away makes the house away.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Already filled in. Open it only if you know you want something else.

data_description.away_delay_min: Advanced: minutes before an empty house counts as away.

notifications.title: What should powerplan tell you?
notifications.description: Three things are worth an interruption; everything else is an entity you can put on a dashboard. A persistent notification always works, even before you have set up a notifier.

data_description.peak_warning: This hour is heading over your capacity target.
data_description.comfort_violation: A room or a tank went below the floor you set.
data_description.notify_service: Which notify service the categories set to Notify use.
data_description.quiet_start: Nothing but the urgent gets through after this.
data_description.quiet_end: Normal notifications resume at this time.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Already filled in. Open it only if you know you want something else.

data_description.peak_uncontrolled: The peak is coming from something powerplan does not steer.
data_description.deadline_at_risk: A charge or a cycle will not finish in time.
data_description.level_up: The month is about to move into a more expensive step.
data_description.price_source_dead: No prices have arrived for a day.
data_description.legionella_at_risk: A water heater's protection cycle cannot complete.
data_description.safe_mode: The engine stopped deciding and released everything.
data_description.force_expired: A manual override ran out and normal control resumed.

review.title: Before powerplan starts

data_description.start_in_observe: Strongly recommended. powerplan decides and explains but writes to nothing, so you can see what it would do before it does it.

error.fuse_out_of_range: A main fuse is between 6 A and 400 A. Check the rating printed on the fuse.
error.phases_not_available: That phase count does not exist on this supply system.
error.power_unit_not_watts: A power sensor has to report watts or kilowatts.
error.eps_looks_like_watts: This looks like watts. The guard band is energy: 0.30 kWh is the default for an hour-long window.
error.eps_not_positive: The guard band has to be more than zero.

abort.already_configured: This meter is already set up as a powerplan site.

unknown_load.message: No load with id {load} on this site.

set_peak_needs_a_day_or_a_month.message: set_peak needs a date or a month.

engine_failing.title: powerplan is in safe mode
engine_failing.description: The engine failed {failures} times in a row ({error}). Every load has been released and the site is observing only. A restart clears safe mode; if it returns, please report the log.

load_error.title: A load failed and is held
load_error.description: The load {load} raised an error during a tick ({error}) and is held in its current state while the other loads continue. Check the device and its bound entities.

meter_stale.title: The grid meter stopped reporting
meter_stale.description: {site}: the grid power reading has been stale for more than ten minutes. The tick is frozen until it returns; check the meter integration.

register_missing.title: No register report for a day
register_missing.description: {site}: the import register has not reported for 24 hours. Windows close on the integral instead; check the meter integration.

scaling_mismatch.title: Power and register disagree
scaling_mismatch.description: {site}: the power integral has been more than 5 % off the register for six windows. One of the two sensors may be scaled wrongly.

price_source_dead.title: A price source is dead
price_source_dead.description: {site}: {source} has not delivered for 24 hours. Prices are synthesised until it returns.

preset_outdated.title: The tariff preset has changed
preset_outdated.description: {site}: the shipped preset {preset} carries other versions than the ones this site was set up with. The site keeps the version it has; reconfigure the tariff to adopt the new one.

bound_helper_missing.title: A bound helper is gone
bound_helper_missing.description: {site}: a schedule, person or calendar this site was bound to no longer exists.

role_missing.title: A required entity is gone
role_missing.description: {site}: an entity a load was bound to no longer exists.

provision_refused.title: A device refuses its provisioning
provision_refused.description: {site}: a device keeps refusing the settings powerplan needs.

legionella_at_risk.title: Legionella cycle at risk
legionella_at_risk.description: {site}: the water heater cannot complete its legionella cycle in time.

delegated_idle.title: A delegated load's controller is silent
delegated_idle.description: {site}: a load left to another controller has not moved for 24 hours.

savings_low_confidence.title: Savings figure is uncertain
savings_low_confidence.description: {site}: a load's counterfactual has missed its calibration for a week; its savings are shown with low confidence.

notify_service_missing.title: Notification service missing
notify_service_missing.description: {site}: the notify service {service} does not exist. Notifications fall back to persistent notifications.

store_reset.title: The store was reset
store_reset.description: {site}: the site's store file could not be read and was moved to {path}. The site started from an empty store; the current window's energy is rebuilt from the register.
